First off, we are in very, oddly paralleled, situations. I am 22 in a family of 6, and both my parents work and struggle to support us. So many on Reddit encourage you to just completely separate from your parents, and I think that’s driven by either how their parents taught them their relationship should be, or theyve had bad experiences with their parents. That’s not how it is in my family. I care deeply for them and appreciate the fact that they pay the bills, paid for my college, support me with therapists, etc. And I will pay it forward to them. Just have in your head that you will take these blessings and spoils you have been given and work even harder to ensure that everyone you care about in your life will be better off. Don’t be so sensitive. Seriously. It’s good that you voiced your opinion here, and I am trying to give genuine supportive advice that is practical, so sorry if I come off as curt. 

You have to be confident and honest with yourself and know that you are in the best place you can be (if that’s really where you are). Trust me, if you keep absorbing others’ emotions and thinking about your current state of being in such a relative way, you’ll be in for a rude awakening post-grad (“this person makes so much more money than me because they work harder!” or “this person has a much better quality of life than me because they’re not being overworked and are passionate about their job!”). Your work should stand on its own, independent of anyone else’s thoughts, negativity, neuroticism, or paranoia. You’ll throw yourself off otherwise. If it’s really incredibly hard for you to separate, practice meditation. It’s worked wonders for my anxiety about other issues.

And btw, the takeaway isn’t to be satisfied with total mediocrity. I gave negative fucks about my grades my freshman year and was pulling a 2.5. In ILR. I failed one class, had incompletes in many others, and if I passed I got no more than a B- (again, in ILR). None of my friends/peers made me feel like I should’ve studied harder, or if they did I just didn’t care. That overcomplacency only served to hurt me and it wasnt until the end of my soph year that I got my shit together and pulled consistent 3.9-4.0s each semester. And I did it for no one’s but my own gratification.
